narrative: Investors should watch whether TSMC confirms the strong AI and advanced-chip demand implied by the Q3 preview’s headline forecast of 65% profit growth, and whether it explains the expected margin slippage toward 50%. The call should also provide detail on pricing, utilization, advanced-node capacity, capital spending, and whether demand from customers such as Nvidia remains robust despite the recent chip-stock volatility. My expectation is a strong quarter and constructive outlook, but with investors likely to focus more on margins and forward capacity constraints than on headline growth alone. Taiwan Semiconductor’s long-term position as a leading foundry remains compelling, though elevated expectations leave the stock vulnerable if management gives cautious guidance.
